sections.title: quick_answer

sections.body_md:
### What each preference pair asks

**E/I — Extraversion and Introversion:** the orientation of attention and energy toward outward engagement or inward reflection. Recall a discussion: did developing thoughts while talking or organizing them before speaking feel preferable? Either approach remains possible. Solitude does not establish poor social skills, and enthusiastic speaking does not rule out Introversion.

**S/N — Sensing and Intuition:** an emphasis on concrete information and experience versus connections, patterns and possibilities. When learning something new, do you first want examples and steps, or consider how it relates to other things? Experience needs interpretation, and ideas need checking. These letters do not rank intelligence, creativity or depth.

**T/F — Thinking and Feeling:** an initial emphasis on logical consistency and impersonal criteria versus values and effects on people when judging. Which standards and whose needs do you want a decision to address? Both approaches can involve reasoning and emotion. Thinking cannot establish a lack of care; Feeling cannot establish an inability to analyze.

**J/P — Judging and Perceiving:** a preference for settling outward arrangements versus openness to incoming information and options. What feels useful to settle now, and what would you rather continue exploring? Deadlines, tasks and responsibilities can require anyone to schedule or adjust. The letters do not measure tidiness, accountability or planning skill.

### Reading a code and the browsing groups

Each position selects a letter from a different pair. INTP, for example, combines I, N, T and P rather than adding four ability scores. Its base profile explains how to read those descriptions together, including occasions that do not fit.

The directory retains NT, NF, SJ and SP browsing groups, combining N/T, N/F, S/J and S/P respectively. Colors and nicknames such as Logician help locate pages; they are not additional measurements or guarantees of an occupation, intelligence, morality or skill. Nicknames can vary across sites. Use the complete code and the framework behind it when comparing information.
sections.title: The four preference pairs

sections.body_md:
### State the reading question, then choose the route

| Your question | Start here | What the page helps explain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What do the letters and the complete description mean? | A base profile, such as [INTP](/en/personality/intp) | Preferences, theoretical interpretation, work and relationships, practice and counterexamples without requiring a suffix. |
| What does INTP-A or INTP-T mean? | [INTP-A](/en/personality/intp-a) or [INTP-T](/en/personality/intp-t) | The additional account of self-evaluation, feedback and pressure, including its limits. |
| How do A and T differ within one type? | [INTP-A vs INTP-T](/en/personality/intp-a-vs-intp-t) | Two descriptions in the same situation, possible costs and observation questions rather than ability rankings. |
| How can I examine two plausible base types? | A cross-type comparison, such as [INTJ vs INTP](/en/personality/intj-vs-intp) or [ISFP vs INFP](/en/personality/isfp-vs-infp) | J/P or S/N in context, without settling type through nicknames, hobbies or a stress response. |
| I want a questionnaire and a result | The [free MBTI test entry](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types) | The specific questionnaire and result explanation; this directory neither scores answers nor produces a result. |

### Keep the base code distinct from A/T

A four-letter profile is readable without a suffix. A (Assertive) and T (Turbulent) belong to the Identity extension in the 16Personalities framework, describing self-assurance, self-evaluation and reactions to pressure. Its instrument is not equivalent to official MBTI. The final T is also distinct from Thinking inside the base code.

Our A/T pages provide educational interpretation and original situations, not validation of your suffix or a prediction of mental health. Base profiles explain the whole type; suffix pages explain the extension; same-type comparisons examine A/T; cross-type comparisons examine the actual differing preferences. Follow the question rather than feel obliged to read every page in sequence. If your result says INTP-T, use the [INTP base profile](/en/personality/intp) for the four letters, then the [INTP-T page](/en/personality/intp-t) for that suffix. If the question is specifically how A and T differ, go directly to their comparison. The pages answer different questions; reading all three cannot verify the result.

### Find the actual difference between two codes

When comparing codes, locate the letter that changes before comparing the nicknames. [ISTJ vs ISFJ](/en/personality/istj-vs-isfj) and [ENFP vs ENTP](/en/personality/enfp-vs-entp) examine T/F: what criteria and effects need to be considered when judging? [ENTJ vs INTJ](/en/personality/entj-vs-intj) examines E/I, including how outward exchange and private reflection enter the same task. The J/P and S/N comparisons in the table have their own questions. [ESTJ vs ENTJ](/en/personality/estj-vs-entj) examines S/N through concrete information, experience and pattern hypotheses, rather than assigning execution and strategy to different people. One episode, such as speaking confidently or changing a plan, cannot settle a preference.

If the directory has no dedicated comparison for your pair, read the two existing base profiles and note their actual differing preferences. A comparison is a way to examine a question, not a ranking of the better type or an instrument for deciding who you are.

### Reading function abbreviations on a detail page

Some detail pages discuss type dynamics using terms such as Introverted Thinking (Ti) or Extraverted Intuition (Ne). These describe a theoretical way of combining the preferences. The attitude in a function name is not a count of conversations, and a proposed stack is not an ability score, brain mechanism or explanation of every stress response. The base pages distinguish official dynamics from differing accounts of the third function's attitude. Read that qualification before treating an online stack diagram as a settled fact.

The A/T extension does not add or replace a function in official MBTI dynamics. Start with the four-letter meaning when abbreviations are unfamiliar; you do not need to master function terminology to use a practical observation question.

### Keep the question and counterexample when type is unsettled

When several accounts feel familiar, state the question you want to clarify and choose the relevant profiles and available comparison. Original reading example: before one discussion you organize thoughts privately; another conversation helps you develop an idea. Examine choices, task demands and experience rather than treat either event as proof of I or E.

Keep a counterexample alongside a familiar description. Record four questions:

- What happened?
- What did you notice or value?
- Which conditions affected the approach?
- What would you try next?

 Instruments, scoring rules and answering conditions can affect results. Recognition or a changed label cannot validate an assessment or establish lasting personality change. Repeated testing is not required to obtain certainty.

If your next question concerns work or a relationship, investigate tasks, skills, qualifications, burdens, needs and limits directly. A profile can help organize a conversation; it cannot screen jobs or partners for you.

### Original reading record: two conflicting results and one specific question

Suppose two tools return ENTJ and INTJ, but your practical question is when discussion or private preparation helps you understand something. Record the tools, versions and answering circumstances first; unavailable details remain unknown. A preferred nickname cannot select the correct result. Read E/I in both full base profiles, then use [ENTJ vs INTJ](/en/personality/entj-vs-intj) for that question. Function abbreviations remain a theoretical layer.

Write one freely chosen occasion when a private outline made explanation easier, and a contrary occasion when someone's question exposed a missing fact. Required immediate replies, different information, staffing or fatigue cannot automatically establish preference. You could agree on advance material and an actually acceptable response window with the people involved, then check whether it helped communication. Proposing the arrangement cannot establish their acceptance.

Reading may clarify terminology, uncertainty and a useful next action. It cannot determine which tool is accurate, establish lasting personality change or certify occupational competence. Stop at the base profile if the four letters answer your question; open the relevant A/T page when the suffix is the question. An unresolved comparison may stay unresolved without repeated testing for a fixed label.
sections.title: Choose the page for your question

items.answer: The four official preference pairs combine into 16 four-letter codes. A/T is a separate extension, giving two suffix descriptions for each code here, rather than changing official MBTI into a 32-type instrument. This site's inventory is 16 base profiles, 32 suffix pages, 16 same-type A/T comparisons, seven cross-type comparisons and this directory: 72 identities, each available in Chinese and English. Counts describe reading pages, not additional measured traits.
items.question: Are there 16 or 32 MBTI types?

items.answer: Yes. A base profile explains the four letters, theory, practical situations and counterexamples without requiring a suffix. Open it when your question concerns the complete type. Read an A/T page only if you want to examine that additional account of self-evaluation and pressure, or go to an A/T comparison when the difference itself is the question. An absent suffix does not make the official four-letter code incomplete.
items.question: Can I read a type without an A/T suffix?

items.answer: The third letter in INTP is T for Thinking, one side of the T/F preference pair. The T after the hyphen means Turbulent in the 16Personalities extension. They occupy different positions, describe different concepts and belong to different frameworks. INTP-T does not mean someone has twice as much Thinking, less Feeling, or an additional official preference. Check which questionnaire produced a result before interpreting either part.
items.question: Why can a Thinking type also be INTP-T?

items.answer: No. Colors and names make the directory easier to browse, and other sites may use different names for the same code. Calling someone a Logician or Commander cannot establish analytical or leadership competence, just as a caring nickname cannot establish professional caring skills. For a work decision, examine the tasks, qualifications, training and demonstrated performance. Use the code to find a page, not the nickname as an occupational recommendation.
items.question: Do the nicknames and colors establish occupational skills?

items.answer: First check whether the results came from the same instrument, version and scoring explanation. Shared letters do not make different questionnaires equivalent, and answering conditions or close scores may complicate interpretation. If those details are unavailable, keep the uncertainty explicit rather than select the label you prefer. Compare a familiar description with a counterexample and the actual circumstances. Reading a profile, recognizing yourself in a story or repeatedly testing until one answer appears cannot validate an assessment; these pages do not settle a conflicting result for you.
items.question: Which result should I trust if tests disagree?

items.answer: No. A comparison can help ask how people obtain information, judge, arrange a task or respond to feedback. It cannot establish skill, eligibility or a successful partnership. For work, investigate requirements, opportunities and constraints; for a relationship, discuss needs, boundaries, responsibilities and the actual behavior in question. The same exercise can be useful when no type is settled. Neither a shared code nor a different one is a reason to screen someone in or out.
items.question: Can a comparison settle career fit or compatibility?

items.answer: Yes. The sources identify the official preference framework, the separate A/T framework and relevant original research or research syntheses. Framework descriptions explain terminology; they are not by themselves empirical proof of a type story. Study findings are limited to their instruments and samples. Original situations are explicitly educational examples, not observations of type populations. The sources and method section explains why favorable consistency estimates, critiques of categorical types and those examples do not establish the validity of a FermatMind result. Follow the source for the particular claim rather than treat the bibliography as support for every sentence.
items.question: Do these pages include research and original sources?

sections.body_md:
The official MBTI describes four preference pairs. A/T belongs to a separate extension; shared letters do not make different tests equivalent. Type narratives and cognitive functions are theoretical interpretations, not established psychological mechanisms.

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self-reports and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19–93; the abstract does not identify a representative country sample. Their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types and found overlap with dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument editions and samples matter: the publisher reports later revisions, and this page does not establish the reliability or validity of a FermatMind score. That specific study does not validate these scenarios, determine an individual's type or settle every question about later instruments.

A newer review by Erford and colleagues (2025) synthesized 193 studies using English-language MBTI Form M, published during 1999–2024. It reported favorable internal-consistency estimates (0.845–0.921) and convergent evidence, while finding no independent structural-validity or test–retest studies in its eligible literature beyond the manual. Score consistency does not establish distinct natural types, validate A/T, or transfer to FermatMind. Both supportive findings and remaining gaps depend on the specific instrument and samples.

The situations and exercises on this page are original educational examples, not clinical guidance or findings about groups. Compare them with your experience, including counterexamples. Do not use type alone to diagnose, hire, choose a career or screen a relationship.

Content revised 8 October 2026. This is a source-based educational synthesis, not a claim of independent clinical review.
